Verdict: needs_cleaning before training.

The dataset is 1200 rows x 24 cols with an explicit binary target (target, cardinality 2, roughly 69/31 split), so the task setup itself is fine. The problems are in feature hygiene:

1) Sentinel values masquerading as data: num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 each cap at max = 9999.0 while their medians sit near 54-62 and std is ~825-846. That is a classic "9999 = missing/unknown" code. Left as-is, these columns will dominate distance/gradient based models, so they must be recoded to NaN (or winsorized/dropped) and then imputed.

2) Missingness: numeric features carry 0-8.6% missing; cat_feature_04/05/06/07 carry 12.7%/13.9%/19.5%/22.1% missing, the worst being cat_feature_07 at 22.1% with 31 categories. That is above a comfortable threshold for simple mode-imputation, and the high-cardinality categoricals (27-31 levels) combined with missingness risk overfitting if one-hot encoded, so target/ordinal encoding with missing as its own level is preferable. The many missing values also appear weakly correlated with the sorted column order, which is worth checking for a data-generation artifact.

3) Outliers: several numeric features show 6-15 IQR outliers (e.g. 15 in num_feature_03, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12), which is tolerable after the 9999 sentinels are fixed.

Nothing here makes the data unusable, but training on it now would import sentinel artifacts and imputation bias, so clean first. Recommended: recode 9999 to missing, choose an explicit imputation/encoding strategy per column, verify the missingness isn't systematic, and confirm the class balance holds after row drops.

Not ready to train as-is; needs cleaning first. Three numeric columns (num_feature_04, num_feature_08, num_feature_12) share a placeholder/sentinel max of 9999.0 while their means (~127-131) and stds (~825-846) are wildly inflated relative to their IQRs (q25-q75 in the 45-70 range near their medians ~54-62). This is characteristic of missing-value sentinels, not real signal, and those columns also carry 4-9% missingness themselves. Separately, seven columns have material missingness, the worst being categorical: cat_feature_07 at 22.1%, cat_feature_06 at 19.5%, cat_feature_05 at 13.9%, cat_feature_04 at 12.7%, and cat_feature_03 at 8.3%; num_feature_14 is highest among numerics at 8.6%. Missingness in the categoricals grows monotonically with cardinality (7 -> 31 levels), which suggests either intentional encoding or non-random dropout and should be tested before imputing. The target itself is clean (2 classes, 0% missing, roughly 69/31 split), so the labels are usable; the work is all in the features. Recommendation: convert the 9999.0 sentinels to NaN, then choose imputation (median for numerics, explicit 'missing' category or most-frequent for low-cardinality categoricals), and verify whether the categorical missing pattern is informative before dropping rows. Outliers flagged by IQR are modest (8-15 per column) and mostly secondary to the sentinels.

Verdict: needs_cleaning before this can be trusted for training.

1) Likely sentinel/censored values. Three numeric columns share a max of exactly 9999.0 (num_feature_04, num_feature_08, num_feature_12) while their q75 values sit around 63-70 and their std (~825-846) is roughly 70x the std of every other numeric column (~11-12). That pattern is a classic placeholder/cap code, not a real measurement. Left as-is these outliers will dominate any distance-based, linear, or tree model. Recommend recoding 9999.0 to NaN and then imputing.

2) Missingness is broad. Several numeric columns have non-trivial gaps (e.g. num_feature_04 8.5%, num_feature_01 2.5%), and the categorical block degrades sharply: cat_feature_04 12.7%, cat_feature_05 13.9%, cat_feature_06 19.5%, cat_feature_07 22.1% missing. Imputing categoricals with an explicit "missing" level is usually safer than mode-filling when missingness may itself be informative. Screening rows with more than ~50% missing features is worth considering.

3) The leakage risk: is_active and signup_date are present with 0 missing. If either was observed at/after the outcome, it will leak and inflate validation scores. Confirm the observation window before including them.

4) Target looks usable: binary with 2 classes, no missing values; the 0.689/0.311 split is mildly imbalanced, so stratify splits and watch accuracy-vs-F1, but no resampling is strictly required.

5) Outliers beyond the sentinel issue are mild: IQR-flag counts of 7-15 per numeric column on 1200 rows are consistent with a heavy-tailed but plausible distribution, and z-score counts are low (1-8). No scaling issues that cleaning wouldn't fix.

Columns are unnamed/unlabeled features (num_feature_*, cat_feature_*) with no domain semantics given, so the sentinel and leakage judgments above are inference-based, hence medium confidence.

The only real open question is whether the missingness and the 9999 sentinels are informative or MCAR — that determines the imputation choice, not whether cleaning is needed. Novelty of outliers looks limited (max z-score counts of 8 or fewer per column), so the extreme values are likely sentinels rather than a heavy-tailed distribution. Confidence is medium because the profile gives no label-leakage check against signup_date or cat_feature_* groupings, and no per-class missingness breakdown.
